subject: general
question: Which of the following rivers marks the eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmaputra river originates from the Angsi Glacier in the Himalayas in Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo River.
 
• It flows eastwards for about 1,700 km through the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, making a U-turn at the Namcha Barwa mountain to enter India in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The river marks the eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas, after which it turns southward into the Assam Valley as the Brahmaputra and further into Bangladesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the major rivers of the Indian subcontinent, with a total length of 2,900 km, making it one of the longest rivers in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kali River**

 
 
• The Kali River, also known as the Sharda River or Mahakali River, flows along the border of India and Nepal.
 
• It originates from the Kalapani springs in the Himalayas at an altitude of 3,600 meters in the Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• The river is significant for both nations, serving as a vital water resource and playing a role in the bilateral treaties between India and Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Teesta River**
 
 
• Teesta River originates from the Tso Lhamo Lake in North Sikkim, India, and flows southward through West Bengal before entering Bangladesh.
 
• It is a major river in the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal, providing water for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
 
 
 
• **Satluj River**
 
 
• The Satluj River, also known as the Sutlej, is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the Punjab region in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• It originates in Tibet near Lake Rakshastal and flows through the Indian states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab before entering Pakistan.
